ei.title: Choose Readers for Critical Insight, Not Closeness
ei.subject: 9월_2026 고2 모의고사
ei.lesson: Choose Readers for Critical Insight, Not Closeness

fullPassage: Only when you're happy that you've done the best you can for your story should you show it to someone else. You may well want to show it to your nearest and dearest, and that's fine, but in most cases you shouldn't look to their reading for any great benefit to your work. The most valuable feedback is likely to come from other sources: you should choose readers for their critical insight, not their closeness to you. Fellow writers are ideal, but don't imagine that any writer will do. If you are part of a writers' circle or class, you'll know whose writing you admire, and if you've had feedback in the past you'll know whose opinions have been helpful ― and whose have not.

questions.passage: Only when you're happy that ①<u>you've done</u> the best you can for your story should you show it to someone else. You may well ②<u>want showing</u> it to your nearest and dearest, and that's fine, but in most cases you shouldn't look to their reading for any great benefit to your work. The most valuable feedback is likely to come from other sources: you should choose readers for their critical insight, not their closeness to you. Fellow writers are ideal, but ③<u>don't imagine</u> that any writer will do. If you are part of a writers' circle or class, you'll know whose writing you admire, and if ④<u>you've had</u> feedback in the past you'll know whose opinions have been helpful ― and whose have not.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ② want showing → want to show: 동사 want는 목적어로 to부정사를 취해요. want to show가 맞습니다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① you've done(해 왔다): 'that you've done the best you can'에서 현재완료(have+과거분사)로 적절해요

✅ ② want showing → want to show: 동사 want(원하다)는 뒤에 동사가 올 때 반드시 'to+동사원형(to부정사)'을 써요. 동명사(-ing)인 showing은 쓸 수 없어서 틀려요 ←정답

❌ ③ don't imagine(상상하지 마라): 'but don't imagine that ~'에서 명령문 부정으로 적절해요

❌ ④ you've had(받아 본 적 있다): 'if you've had feedback in the past'에서 현재완료로 적절해요
det.tip: want / hope / decide / plan 등은 뒤에 to부정사! (want to show, want to go)

questions.passage: Only when you're happy that you've done the best you can for your story should you show it to someone else. You may well want to show it to your nearest and dearest, and that's fine, but in most cases you ①<u>shouldn't look</u> to their reading for any great benefit to your work. The most valuable feedback is likely to come from other sources: you should choose readers for their critical insight, not their closeness to you. Fellow writers are ideal, but ②<u>don't imagine</u> that any writer will do. ③<u>If you will be part of</u> a writers' circle or class, you'll know whose writing you admire, and if ④<u>you've had</u> feedback in the past you'll know whose opinions have been helpful ― and whose have not.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③ If you will be part of → If you are part of: 조건을 나타내는 if절에서는 미래의 일도 현재시제로 써요. will을 빼고 are가 맞습니다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① shouldn't look(기대하면 안 된다): 'shouldn't+동사원형'으로 적절해요

❌ ② don't imagine(상상하지 마라): 명령문 부정으로 적절해요

✅ ③ If you will be part of → If you are part of: '만약 ~라면'이라는 조건의 if절 안에서는 미래 내용이라도 will을 쓰지 않고 현재시제로 나타내요. 그래서 will be가 아니라 are가 맞아요 ←정답

❌ ④ you've had(받아 본 적 있다): 'if you've had feedback in the past'에서 현재완료로 적절해요
det.tip: 때·조건의 부사절(when, if 등)에서는 미래를 현재시제로! (If you are ~, you'll know ~)

questions.passage: Only when you're happy that you've done the best you can for your story should you ①<u>show them to someone else</u>. You may well want to show it to your nearest and dearest, and that's fine, but in most cases you ②<u>shouldn't look</u> to their reading for any great benefit to your work. The most valuable feedback is likely to come from other sources: you should choose readers for their critical insight, not their closeness to you. Fellow writers are ideal, but don't imagine ③<u>that any writer will do</u>. If you are part of a writers' circle or class, you'll know whose writing you admire, and if ④<u>you've had</u> feedback in the past you'll know whose opinions have been helpful ― and whose have not.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ① show them → show it: 가리키는 대상이 'your story(당신의 이야기)'로 단수이므로 대명사는 단수 it이 맞습니다. them(복수)은 틀려요.
det.analysis:
✅ ① show them to someone else → show it to someone else: 여기서 보여 주는 대상은 앞의 'your story(당신의 이야기)' 한 편이에요. 단수라서 대명사는 it을 써야 하고, 복수 them은 틀려요 ←정답

❌ ② shouldn't look(기대하면 안 된다): 'shouldn't+동사원형'으로 적절해요

❌ ③ that any writer will do(아무 작가나 괜찮다는 것): 'imagine that ~'의 명사절 접속사 that으로 적절해요

❌ ④ you've had(받아 본 적 있다): 현재완료로 적절해요
det.tip: 대명사는 가리키는 명사의 수와 맞춰요. story(단수) → it / stories(복수) → them

questions.passage: Only when you're ①<u>happy</u> that you've done the best you can for your story should you show it to someone else. You may well want to show it to your nearest and dearest, and that's ②<u>fine</u>, but in most cases you shouldn't look to their reading for any great benefit to your ③<u>work</u>. ④<u>The least valuable</u> feedback is likely to come from other sources: you should choose readers for their critical insight, not their closeness to you. Fellow writers are ideal, but don't imagine that any writer will do. If you are part of a writers' circle or class, you'll know whose writing you admire, and if you've had feedback in the past you'll know whose opinions have been helpful ― and whose have not.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ The least valuable → The most valuable: 글은 '가장 값진 피드백은 다른 출처에서 온다'고 하므로 '가장(most)'이 맞아요. '가장 덜 값진(least)'은 정반대예요.
det.analysis:
✅ ① happy(만족하는): '최선을 다했다고 만족할 때'로 적절해요

✅ ② fine(괜찮은): '그것도 괜찮다(that's fine)'로 적절해요

✅ ③ work(작품·글): '당신의 작품에 큰 도움'으로 적절해요

❌ ④ The least valuable(가장 덜 값진) → The most valuable(가장 값진): 뒤에서 '예리한 통찰을 지닌 독자를 고르라'며 좋은 피드백을 강조하므로, 여기는 '가장 값진(most)' 피드백이어야 해요. '가장 덜 값진'은 흐름과 반대예요 ←정답
det.tip: the most valuable = 가장 값진. 글 전체가 '좋은 피드백 찾기'라 최상급 most가 맞아요.

questions.passage: Only when you're ①<u>happy</u> that you've done the best you can for your story should you show it to someone else. You may well want to show it to your nearest and dearest, and that's fine, but in most cases you shouldn't look to their reading for any great benefit to your work. The most valuable feedback is likely to come from ②<u>familiar</u> sources: you should choose readers for their critical insight, not their closeness to you. Fellow writers are ③<u>ideal</u>, but don't imagine that any writer will do. If you are part of a writers' circle or class, you'll know whose writing you ④<u>admire</u>, and if you've had feedback in the past you'll know whose opinions have been helpful ― and whose have not.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ② familiar → other: 값진 피드백은 나와 가까운 사람이 아니라 '다른(other)' 출처에서 나온다는 흐름이라 other가 맞아요. familiar(친숙한)는 정반대예요.
det.analysis:
✅ ① happy(만족하는): '만족할 때'로 적절해요

❌ ② familiar(친숙한) → other(다른): 바로 뒤에서 '가까움(closeness)이 아니라 비판적 통찰로 독자를 고르라'고 해요. 즉 값진 피드백은 친숙한 사람이 아니라 '다른' 출처에서 온다는 뜻이라 other가 맞고, '친숙한(familiar)'은 흐름과 반대예요 ←정답

✅ ③ ideal(이상적인): '동료 작가가 이상적'으로 적절해요

✅ ④ admire(존경하다): '누구의 글을 존경하는지'로 적절해요
det.tip: come from other sources = 다른 출처에서 나오다. '친숙한'과는 정반대 방향이에요.

questions.passage: Only when you're happy that you've done the best you can for your story should you show it to someone else. You may well want to show it to your nearest and dearest, and that's fine, but in most cases you shouldn't look to their reading for __________ to your work. The most valuable feedback is likely to come from other sources: you should choose readers for their critical insight, not their closeness to you. Fellow writers are ideal, but don't imagine that any writer will do. If you are part of a writers' circle or class, you'll know whose writing you admire, and if you've had feedback in the past you'll know whose opinions have been helpful ― and whose have not.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 빈칸은 'their reading for ___ to your work'로, 가까운 사람의 감상에서 작품에 큰 '이득'을 기대하지 말라는 흐름입니다.
det.analysis:
빈칸 뒤 'to your work(당신의 작품에)'와 이어져 '작품에 도움이 되는 무언가'가 와야 하고, 뒤 문장의 'valuable feedback(값진 피드백)'과도 연결돼요.

✅ ① any great benefit(큰 이득): '가까운 이의 감상에서 작품에 큰 이득을 기대하지 말라'로 자연스러워요 ←정답

❌ ② much personal comfort(많은 개인적 위안): 위안이 아니라 작품에 대한 '도움'이 핵심이라 어색해요

❌ ③ a quick reply(빠른 답장): 응답 속도는 글의 초점이 아니에요

❌ ④ any special payment(특별한 대가): 돈·보상 이야기는 본문에 없어요
det.tip: look to A for benefit = A에서 이득을 기대하다. 작품(work)에 대한 도움이 핵심이에요.

questions.passage: Only when you're happy that you've done the best you can for your story should you show it to someone else. You may well want to show it to your nearest and dearest, and that's fine, but in most cases you shouldn't look to their reading for any great benefit to your work. The most valuable feedback is likely to come from other sources: you should choose readers for their critical insight, not their closeness to you. Fellow writers are ideal, but don't imagine that __________. If you are part of a writers' circle or class, you'll know whose writing you admire, and if you've had feedback in the past you'll know whose opinions have been helpful ― and whose have not.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: '동료 작가가 이상적이지만(but) ___라고 생각하지 마라'는 흐름이므로, 아무 작가나 다 괜찮은 것은 아니라는 내용이 와야 합니다.
det.analysis:
앞에서 'Fellow writers are ideal(동료 작가가 이상적)'이라고 한 뒤 but으로 뒤집으므로, 빈칸에는 '그렇다고 아무나 다 되는 건 아니다'라는 경고가 와야 해요.

❌ ① every reader is honest(모든 독자가 정직하다): 정직함은 초점이 아니에요

❌ ② your family will help(당신의 가족이 도와줄 것이다): 가족 이야기는 앞 문장에서 이미 다뤘어요

✅ ③ any writer will do(아무 작가나 다 괜찮다): 'don't imagine that any writer will do(아무 작가나 괜찮다고 생각하지 마라)'로 but 뒤 반전과 딱 맞아요 ←정답

❌ ④ all feedback is useful(모든 피드백이 유용하다): 피드백 전반이 아니라 '작가 선택'이 초점이에요
det.tip: 여기서 will do는 '충분하다·괜찮다'의 뜻. any writer will do = 아무 작가나 괜찮다.

questions.passage: Only when you're happy that you've done the best you can for your story should you show it to someone else. You may well want to show it to your nearest and dearest, and that's fine, but in most cases you shouldn't look to their reading for any great benefit to your work. The most valuable feedback is likely to come from other sources: you should choose readers for their critical insight, not their closeness to you. Fellow writers are ideal, but don't imagine that any writer will do. If you are part of a writers' circle or class, you'll know whose writing you admire, and if you've had feedback in the past you'll know whose opinions have been helpful ― and whose have not.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: 본문: Only when you're happy that you've done the best you can for your story should you show it to someone else — 최선을 다했다고 만족할 때에만 보여 주라는 내용.
det.analysis:
✅ ① 첫 문장에서 '자신의 글에 최선을 다했다고 만족할 때에만' 남에게 보여 주라고 했어요 ←정답

❌ ② '최선을 다한 뒤에' 보여 주라고 했으므로 '검토 없이 곧바로 공개'는 반대예요

❌ ③ 뒤에서 가까운 사람에게 보여 줘도 괜찮고 좋은 독자를 고르라고 했으므로 '누구에게도 보여 주지 마라'는 반대예요

❌ ④ '낯선 사람에게 먼저'라는 순서는 본문에 없어요
det.tip: Only when ~ = 오직 ~할 때에만. 만족스러울 만큼 다듬은 뒤가 그 시점이에요.

ch: 글쓴이는 스스로 최선을 다했다고 느낄 때 비로소 글을 남에게 보여 주라고 조언한다.
초고가 완성되면 검토 없이 곧바로 공개하는 것이 좋다.
자신의 글은 누구에게도 보여 주지 않는 편이 낫다.
글은 반드시 낯선 사람에게 먼저 보여 주어야 한다.

questions.passage: Only when you're happy that you've done the best you can for your story should you show it to someone else. You may well want to show it to your nearest and dearest, and that's fine, but in most cases you shouldn't look to their reading for any great benefit to your work. The most valuable feedback is likely to come from other sources: you should choose readers for their critical insight, not their closeness to you. Fellow writers are ideal, but don't imagine that any writer will do. If you are part of a writers' circle or class, you'll know whose writing you admire, and if you've had feedback in the past you'll know whose opinions have been helpful ― and whose have not.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.korean: 본문: in most cases you shouldn't look to their reading for any great benefit to your work — 가까운 사람의 감상에서 큰 도움을 기대하지 말라고 함.
det.analysis:
❌ ① '최선을 다했다고 느낄 때 보여 주라'는 첫 문장과 일치해요

❌ ② '동료 작가가 이상적(Fellow writers are ideal)'이라는 내용과 일치해요

✅ ③ 본문은 '대부분의 경우 가까운 이의 감상에서 큰 도움을 기대하지 말라'고 했어요. '대체로 큰 도움을 준다'는 정반대라 일치하지 않아요 ←정답

❌ ④ '친밀함이 아니라 비판적 통찰로 독자를 고르라'와 일치해요
det.tip: shouldn't look for any great benefit = 큰 도움을 기대하지 마라. 이 문장을 뒤집은 선지예요.

ch: 최선을 다했다고 느낀 뒤 글을 공개하는 것이 바람직하다.
동료 작가는 좋은 피드백 상대가 될 수 있다.
가까운 사람의 감상은 대체로 작품에 큰 도움을 준다.
독자는 친밀함보다 예리한 통찰을 기준으로 골라야 한다.

questions.passage: Only when you're happy that you've done the best you can for your story should you show it to someone else. You may well want to show it to your nearest and dearest, and that's fine, but in most cases you shouldn't look to their reading for any great benefit to your work. The most valuable feedback is likely to come from other sources: you should choose readers for their critical insight, not their closeness to you. Fellow writers are ideal, but don't imagine that any writer will do. If you are part of a writers' circle or class, you'll know whose writing you admire, and if you've had feedback in the past you'll know whose opinions have been helpful ― and whose have not.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: 본문: Fellow writers are ideal, but don't imagine that any writer will do — 동료 작가는 이상적이지만 아무 작가나 다 되는 것은 아님.
det.analysis:
❌ ① '아무 작가나 다 되는 건 아니다(don't imagine that any writer will do)'라고 했으므로 '누구나 훌륭한 피드백을 준다'는 반대예요

✅ ② '동료 작가는 이상적(ideal)'이라고 분명히 밝혔어요 ←정답

❌ ③ '친밀함이 아니라 비판적 통찰로 고르라'고 했으므로 '친밀함이 더 중요'는 반대예요

❌ ④ '큰 도움을 기대하지 말라'고 했으므로 '늘 큰 도움'은 반대예요
det.tip: Fellow writers are ideal = 동료 작가가 이상적이다. 단, 아무나는 아니에요.

ch: 글을 쓰는 사람이라면 누구나 훌륭한 피드백을 줄 수 있다.
동료 작가는 이상적인 피드백 상대가 될 수 있다.
독자를 고를 때는 통찰보다 나와의 친밀함이 더 중요하다.
가까운 사람의 반응에서 늘 큰 도움을 기대할 수 있다.

questions.passage: Only when you're happy that you've done the best you can for your story should you show it to someone else. You may well want to show it to your nearest and dearest, and that's fine, but in most cases you shouldn't look to their reading for any great benefit to your work. The most valuable feedback is likely to come from other sources: you should choose readers for their critical insight, not their closeness to you. Fellow writers are ideal, but don't imagine that any writer will do. If you are part of a writers' circle or class, you'll know whose writing you admire, and if you've had feedback in the past you'll know whose opinions have been helpful ― and whose have not.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 글 전체가 '누구에게 피드백을 받을 것인가', 즉 피드백 제공자를 고르는 기준을 다룹니다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① 가족의 정서적 지지: 가까운 사람 이야기는 일부일 뿐 중심이 아니에요

questions.passage: Only when you're happy that you've done the best you can for your story should you show it to someone else. You may well want to show it to your nearest and dearest, and that's fine, but in most cases you shouldn't look to their reading for any great benefit to your work. The most valuable feedback is likely to come from other sources: you should choose readers for their critical insight, not their closeness to you. Fellow writers are ideal, but don't imagine that any writer will do. If you are part of a writers' circle or class, you'll know whose writing you admire, and if you've had feedback in the past you'll know whose opinions have been helpful ― and whose have not.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 핵심 주장(친밀함이 아니라 비판적 통찰을 기준으로 독자를 고르라)을 담은 제목이 적절합니다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① Show Your Story to Everyone Right Away(당신의 이야기를 즉시 모두에게 보여 줘라): 최선을 다한 뒤 신중히 보여 주라는 내용과 반대예요

✅ ② Choose Your Readers for Insight, Not Closeness(친밀함이 아니라 통찰을 기준으로 독자를 골라라): 글의 핵심 주장 그대로예요 ←정답

❌ ③ Why Family Feedback Matters Most(가족의 피드백이 가장 중요한 이유): 가족의 감상엔 큰 기대를 말라고 했으니 반대예요

❌ ④ The Fastest Way to Finish a Novel(소설을 가장 빨리 끝내는 법): 완성 속도는 다루지 않아요
det.tip: 제목 = 주제를 한 문장으로 압축한 것. 'insight, not closeness'가 핵심이에요.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: have(you've) 뒤에는 과거분사가 오는 현재완료이므로, 동사 do를 과거분사 done으로 바꿔야 합니다.
det.analysis:
빈칸 앞에 'you've(= you have)'가 있어요. 'have + 과거분사'는 현재완료(~해 왔다)를 만들어요.

동사 do의 과거분사는 done이에요. (do - did - done)

→ you've done the best you can = 당신이 할 수 있는 최선을 다했다.

did(과거형)를 쓰면 have 뒤에 올 수 없어 틀려요. 반드시 과거분사 done이어야 해요.
det.tip: have/has 뒤에는 과거분사! do의 과거분사는 done (do-did-done).

det.tip: come from other sources, not their closeness = 가까움이 아니라 다른 출처에서. 이 대조를 뒤집은 선지예요.
